Why Andover Homes Need Custom Home Building

Andover's climate puts real demands on residential construction. With 76 freeze days per year and 36 freeze-thaw cycles annually, foundations and exterior materials face constant expansion and contraction that can compromise structural integrity over time. The average high of 68°F and low of 49°F create significant temperature swings, while 35 inches of annual rainfall and 11 inches of snowfall test roofing systems and drainage solutions throughout the year.

Butler County has faced 100 federal disaster declarations in the last decade alone—99 severe storm events and one fire emergency. When you're building in USDA Plant Hardiness Zone 6b, where winter temperatures can drop to -5°F, every construction decision matters. Andover sits in FEMA Flood Zone X, offering minimal flood risk outside the 500-year floodplain, but that doesn't eliminate the need for proper grading and water management around your custom home.

The 5,341 housing units in Andover represent families who chose this community for its schools, parks, and growing entertainment options. Custom home building here isn't about following trends—it's about creating a residence designed specifically for your family's needs, built to endure the weather patterns monitored by the NWS ICT office and KICT radar system that tracks Butler County conditions.
